taxonomy.subtopic: Accelerated follicular atresia, streak ovaries and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism

questions.stem_html: A 15-year-old girl is evaluated for primary amenorrhea. She is short, has a broad chest and low posterior hairline, and has not developed breasts. Pelvic ultrasonography shows a small uterus and streak-like gonads. Laboratory testing shows low estradiol with markedly elevated follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone. Which process best explains this hormone pattern?

options.text_html: Excess ovarian inhibin production suppressing follicle-stimulating hormone
Accelerated loss of ovarian follicles causing reduced estrogen feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary
Persistent anti-Müllerian hormone secretion from functioning testes
Pituitary destruction with deficient gonadotropin release
Failure of hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion

questions.explanation_html: In Turner syndrome, accelerated degeneration of ovarian follicles begins during fetal life and commonly produces fibrous streak gonads and primary ovarian insufficiency. Low estradiol removes negative feedback from the hypothalamus and pituitary, so gonadotropins rise. This is hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Hypothalamic GnRH deficiency causes low or inappropriately normal FSH and LH rather than markedly elevated gonadotropins.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Pituitary destruction also causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with low gonadotropin concentrations.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Inhibin suppresses FSH, but streak ovaries lack functioning follicles and therefore do not produce excess inhibin.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Anti-Müllerian hormone from testes explains absent Müllerian structures in a 46,XY disorder, not a patient with a uterus and Turner phenotype.

questions.educational_objective: Turner syndrome causes accelerated follicular atresia and streak ovaries; loss of ovarian estrogen and inhibin feedback produces hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.

media.alt_text: Original hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis diagram showing streak ovaries, low estradiol and loss of negative feedback with elevated FSH and LH.
